headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from shared note-to-document workflow; no direct data-leak or capability-conflict pathway is evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can use RAG/web-search outputs, while marker processes documents. If marker ingests Khoj-produced text or notes from the shared index, attacker-controlled content could be reinterpreted as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is a plausible but not proven default pathway.
conditions: IF marker consumes Khoj-generated text as instructions or prompts
IF both agents are pointed at the same note/document corpus without provenance labels
mitigations: Add a provenance header to all Khoj outputs before passing them to marker
Strip instructions from retrieved text before document processing
Use separate folders for raw notes and generated summaries
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like content
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents and has broad network egress, but marker has no filesystem read surface and no network egress. The pair does not show a shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage from Khoj into marker is not evidenced beyond limited manual transfer risk.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies personal notes from Khoj into marker inputs
IF marker is configured to process files containing sensitive notes from Khoj
mitigations: Avoid passing personal notes into marker unless necessary
Redact sensitive fields before document processing
Use a separate non-sensitive test document
Confirm marker runs on local-only inputs
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between the two tools

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and marker likewise cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource exposed in the profiles, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to gain write access to the same directory
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents shared mutable state
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only
Do not mount a shared writable workspace
Recheck permissions after upgrades
Use separate output directories
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can generate retrieved answers from indexed notes, and marker is a document-processing system that may render or transform upstream text. If marker treats Khoj output as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream documents. The profiles do not show explicit verification or action-taking safeguards.
conditions: IF marker uses Khoj-generated summaries as source text without verification
IF downstream documents are produced from Khoj output verbatim
mitigations: Require a human review step before reuse
Mark Khoj output as untrusted source text
Compare generated claims against original documents
Limit marker to formatting, not fact extraction
requires-engineering: add citation-preserving verification

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, which can carry residency or retention obligations, while marker's profile shows no data classes or residency constraints. The pair does not document a compliance mismatch, so only a small gap exists if regulated notes are manually routed through marker.
conditions: IF regulated personal notes are exported from Khoj into marker
IF marker is used on data subject to stricter retention than Khoj's handling
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of marker
Document retention for any exported files
Delete temporary exports after processing
Use synthetic samples for testing
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
